Issue ID: 40076192

Author: fa...@gmail.com
<p><strong>VULNERABILITY DETAILS</strong><br>
Extensions can be used to download URLs of internal pages or blocked URL, bypassing both URLBlocklists and ExtensionSetting runtime_blocked_hosts policies set by the Enterprise.</p>
<p><strong>VERSION</strong><br>
Chrome Version: 119.0.6045.105 (Official Build) (64-bit)<br>
Operating System: Linux</p>
<p>To set up Enterprise policy of Chrome on other platforms, see:<br>
* Windows - <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7532015" data-b-widget="url" data-b-original-href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7532015" data-b-redirected-href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7532015&amp;sa=D&amp;source=buganizer&amp;usg=AOvVaw3FP_1EVTaqaRPgQk9j4NXy">https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7532015</a><br>
* macOS - <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7517624" data-b-widget="url" data-b-original-href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7517624" data-b-redirected-href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7517624&amp;sa=D&amp;source=buganizer&amp;usg=AOvVaw1e5mLtq_BTnNVpVE-Zc2km">https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7517624</a><br>
* Linux - <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7517525" data-b-widget="url" data-b-original-href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7517525" data-b-redirected-href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7517525&amp;sa=D&amp;source=buganizer&amp;usg=AOvVaw1RJ-B4B7xGsHh4OBwXaGU2">https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7517525</a></p>
<p><strong>REPRODUCTION CASE</strong></p>
<ol>
<li>Download the attached files (manifest.json, background.js) and put it in a directory - the extension directory.</li>
<li>Create an enterprise policy to block a domain, such as sysinternals.com (here used to download <a href="https://download.sysinternals.com/files/SysinternalsSuite.zip" data-b-widget="url" data-b-original-href="https://download.sysinternals.com/files/SysinternalsSuite.zip" data-b-redirected-href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://download.sysinternals.com/files/SysinternalsSuite.zip&amp;sa=D&amp;source=buganizer&amp;usg=AOvVaw3UryNWDIUDEDnfcy8C1yHi">https://download.sysinternals.com/files/SysinternalsSuite.zip</a>).<br>
To configure on Chromium for Linux, see <a href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7517525" data-b-widget="url" data-b-original-href="https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7517525" data-b-redirected-href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7517525&amp;sa=D&amp;source=buganizer&amp;usg=AOvVaw1RJ-B4B7xGsHh4OBwXaGU2">https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7517525</a>, create a policy using any below settings to test:</li>
</ol>
<p>{<br>
&quot;URLBlocklist&quot;: [&quot;sysinternals.com&quot;]<br>
}</p>
<p>or</p>
<p>{<br>
&quot;ExtensionSettings&quot;: {<br>
&quot;*&quot;: {<br>
&quot;runtime_blocked_hosts&quot;: [&quot;*://*.sysinternals.com&quot;],<br>
&quot;blocked_permissions&quot;: []<br>
}<br>
}<br>
}</p>
<ol start="3">
<li>Load the extension for testing</li>
</ol>

Author: Hi fazmin.pentester@. Thanks for tracking this issue. Sorry for my delayed response because I was just back from a long leave.

The URLBlocklist policy is not designed to block the download from an extension because it only affect page loading in the Chrome browser. See more description from this offical doc: https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#URLBlocklist

It looks like ExtensionSettings.runtime_blocked_hosts may be designed to block such a download, but I am not 100% sure. Reassign this bug to the policy owner finnur@ to take a look and confirm whether this behavior is intended or not.
TmpkbU5ESmxNVEpsWkRFd1lURTVaalkyWVRka1lqaGlNVFl6WTJNeU1qWT0=

Author: fa...@gmail.com
[I would also like to report]<br>Using resource loading, a user can locally obtain the content of blocked internal URLs, and a remote attacker can potentially leak enterprise-blocked internal URLs by loading them as resources and fetching them using the devtool.getResources function.<br><br>Any user could expose blocked internal pages through HTML sourceMappingURL injection.<br><br>proof-of-concept: `data:text/html,&lt;body&gt;Open DevTools&lt;/body&gt;&lt;script&gt;//%23%20sourceMappingURL=data:application/json,{&quot;version&quot;:3,&quot;sources&quot;:[&quot;<a href="https://google.com/robots.txt" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow ugc" data-b-widget="url" data-b-original-href="https://google.com/robots.txt" data-b-redirected-href="https://google.com/robots.txt">https://google.com/robots.txt</a>&quot;]}&lt;/script&gt;` (Here, we will use the example URL &quot;<a href="https://google.com/robots.txt" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow ugc" data-b-widget="url" data-b-original-href="https://google.com/robots.txt" data-b-redirected-href="https://google.com/robots.txt">https://google.com/robots.txt</a>&quot; as a sensitive enterprise internal/blocked URL for demonstration, where the current user shouldn&#39;t have access to this file.)<br><br>Furthermore, this vulnerability can be further exploited by a malicious browser extension to transmit this information to a remote attacker.

TUdSa1lXSTNaVEJrTUdVNE9HSXhNbU0yTVRReVlqTmlZMkU1T1RjMlpUaz0=

Author: Hmm... I'm not sure if this is a security bug.

This allows the extension to _download_ files from blocked URLs, but it can't _access_ those files without having file access to the machine (and if it has file access to the machine, most bets are off).  The runtime blocked hosts policy restricts which web pages an extension can access, but that's distinct from what's happening here.  Additionally, even if we blocked access to runtime_blocked_hosts via the chrome.downloads API (which is fairly doable), extensions could still trigger downloads from these via the tabs API or other forms of navigation, depending on how the server chose to respond to the request.  And blocking access to runtime blocked hosts in every API that could feasibly trigger navigation would be very detrimental to a lot of valid use cases (like tab, window, history, bookmark managers).

I'll zmin@ here as an owner of enterprise policies, but I think this might be one we close out as WAI.
TUdSa1lXSTNaVEJrTUdVNE9HSXhNbU0yTVRReVlqTmlZMkU1T1RjMlpUaz0=

Author: zm...@chromium.org
<p>This issue is a bit old and some files are expired so I can&#39;t see how this file got downloaded. I assume it&#39;s an extension got loaded and that extension accesses an URL which automatically download a file.</p>
<p>In general, like Anqing and Devlin said above, neither URLBlocklist nor ExtensionSettings is designed to prevent downloading. URLBlocklist can block user navigation while ExtensionSettings controls which page an extension can have access to. Those policies may block download in some situations but clearly not all of them.</p>
<p>There is a different set of policies for download control. A simple one is to use <a href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DownloadRestrictions" data-b-widget="url" data-b-original-href="https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DownloadRestrictions" data-b-redirected-href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/%23DownloadRestrictions&amp;sa=D&amp;source=buganizer&amp;usg=AOvVaw1OQz92WDP1dEzvpRbozv4F">DownloadRestrictions</a> policy. Set it to 3 should block all download. We also provides more complicated download control as an advanced security feature.</p>
